llm_summary: The run gained strong early tempo from Neow's Lament and several useful control cards, but it entered the Hexaghost fight with only 57 HP and no remaining potions. The final deck had reasonable defensive tools, yet the boss fight repeatedly ended turns with little or no block while Burn+ cards accumulated, and the run died with Hexaghost still at 68 HP. The clearest improvement is to value exhaust/draw options more highly against Hexaghost and apply a stricter survival check during low-HP attack turns.

llm_lessons.title: Value exhaust and draw against Burn-heavy bosses
llm_lessons.situation: When Act 1 card rewards offer exhaust, draw, and multi-card defensive effects, especially before Hexaghost.
llm_lessons.lesson: Do not automatically prefer a single-card defensive tool such as True Grit or Shrug It Off; give substantial weight to options like Second Wind or Burning Pact that can remove Burn cards, improve hand quality, or generate more block over a whole turn.
evidence_points: At Floor 13, True Grit was chosen over Second Wind; at Floor 14, Shrug It Off was chosen over Burning Pact.
The final build contained True Grit and Shrug It Off but not Second Wind or Burning Pact.
During the Hexaghost fight, the logged hands repeatedly contained multiple Burn+ cards, including four Burn+ cards on Turn 12 and three on Turn 14.
llm_lessons.reasoning: The final boss hand state shows that Burn cards consumed a large part of future draws. The rejected alternatives offered ways to exhaust those cards or improve hand throughput, so future reward evaluations should account for Hexaghost's persistent status burden rather than judging block cards only by their immediate effect.

llm_lessons.title: Use a survival threshold when low HP meets an attack intent
llm_lessons.situation: When below roughly half health and the enemy is attacking, particularly if the hand contains both defensive and offensive cards.
llm_lessons.lesson: Before playing another attack, check whether the turn leaves enough block to survive the next hit; if not, prioritize every legal defensive line and only add damage when it is necessary to prevent a worse outcome.
evidence_points: On Turn 11, the player had 35 HP against an ATTACK intent and the sequence ended after Battle Trance, Headbutt, Defend, and True Grit with only 5 block.
On Turn 12, the player had 29 HP against ATTACK_DEBUFF and ended the sequence with Defend after spending the turn on Battle Trance and Bash.
By Turn 14, the player had 10 HP and used Defend before Dropkick while Hexaghost had ATTACK intent, ending with only 5 block and Hexaghost still at 68 HP.
llm_lessons.reasoning: The log does not establish the exact incoming damage or prove a single missed card would have saved the fight, so this is a cautious combat heuristic rather than a definite counterfactual. However, the repeated combination of very low HP, attack intents, and minimal end-of-turn block shows that future play should explicitly test survival before committing energy to marginal damage.

llm_lessons.title: Repeat the early Neow's Lament tempo line
llm_lessons.situation: When Neow offers the choice to make the next three combats nearly free and the route can immediately reach several early rewards.
llm_lessons.lesson: The one-HP-enemy blessing is a strong Act 1 tempo option: use the safe early fights to collect card rewards and event value while preserving HP for later elites and the boss.
evidence_points: The run chose the blessing that made enemies in the next three combats have 1 HP.
The first three logged combats ended with enemies at 1 HP, and the player remained at 80 HP after the first combat and 77 HP after the second.
The run used that safety to take Headbutt and Battle Trance and remove a Strike at the early event.
llm_lessons.reasoning: The blessing directly converted the opening combats into low-risk rewards and enabled early deck improvement without spending significant HP. This was one of the run's successful strategic choices and is worth repeating when the early route supports it.
